newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds consolidate after data sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds consolidate after data sell-off.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were just above the highs seen in after-hours trading as the market attempted to consolidate Wednesday's post-CPI data sell-off.
*March motor registraions due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond yields were just below the highs seen in after-hours trading as the market attempted to consolidate Wednesday's post-CPI data sell-off.

Although the March quarter data showed inflation remaining extremely subdued, speculative buying in anticipation of it being even more favourable than the consensus saw the debt market subsequently battered by profit-taking.

"You also had a lot of people squaring up ahead of the long weekend," one trader added. Friday's ANZAC day is a national holiday. "I don't expect we are going to see too much today and we'll probably hold tight ranges as we try and consolidate."

The subdued inflation outcome, combined with the moderate A$10 per week pay award granted by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission earlier this week, is seen by some analysts as a window of opportunity for the Reserve Bank to ease policy if it felt that the economy needed a further stimulus.

However, a majority of economists see the data as merely relieving any pressure that there might have been on the RBA to raise official interest rates, which is now seen as an unlikely event until next year when growth should be in full swing.
Headline inflation rose 0.2 percent in the latest quarter while underlying inflation rose 0.4 percent.

Next week's data will give a better idea of current activity in the economy with retail trade and building approvals for March, along with the key quarterly average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE).
There is also a busy data week in the United States, which includes first quarter GDP, the National Association of Purchasing Management Index and non-farm payrolls.
U.S. Treasuries weakened on Wednesday after a solid response to a five-year note auction failed to follow-through in the secondary market.

Spread differentials to the dollar bloc showed only modest movements after Wednesday's wild swings. Canadian debt slightly outperformed the U.S. market on Wednesday, underpinned by gains in the Canadian dollar, while the short end of the New Zealand curve was buoyed by a firm N.Z. trade weighted index.
